raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
# Description

Validate grouped split sizes inside the existing device-side multi-output offset scan. GroupedLinear requests 128-row alignment; the generic grouped MLP offset path requests 256-row alignment. The check runs on every CUDA graph replay without a host read or an added kernel launch.

`nvte_splits_to_offsets_multi_v2(split_sizes, split_alignment, outputs, ...)` exposes the check. The original C API symbol remains and forwards with alignment 1. The PyTorch private binding accepts an optional `split_alignment`. 


## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Changes

- Validate every device-resident split in the prefix-sum kernel, including later 256-element scan chunks. `NVTE_DEVICE_ERROR` prints and asserts; `__trap()` keeps the failure effective in Release builds where `NDEBUG` removes the assert. `NVTE_BUILD_DEBUG=1` enables the assert when building, not at runtime.
- Use a bitmask for power-of-two alignments and run the existing scan with 128 threads for up to 128 splits, retaining 256 threads for larger inputs.
- Pass alignment from GroupedLinear and grouped MLP into the multi-output scan.
- Keep the device-trap failure case out of the automated tests because it invalidates the test process's CUDA context. Existing grouped tensor tests pass; this PR has no negative alignment regression test.
- Document the device-side alignment contract.

### Offset-scan GPU time on GB200

Measured the one- and four-output scan with 8 and 16 experts, 256 rows per expert, and `split_alignment=128` on the PR. The four-output call uses strides `[1,1,7168,4096]`, matching a grouped linear FC1 shape. Inputs are CUDA int64 splits; the first output is int32 and the remaining outputs are int64. Four-output calls use bulk allocation.

| Experts | Outputs | Base µs/call | PR µs/call | PR − Base µs |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8 | 1 | 2.884 | 2.913 | +0.029 |
| 16 | 1 | 2.883 | 2.912 | +0.028 |
| 8 | 4 | 3.651 | 3.648 | −0.003 |
| 16 | 4 | 3.651 | 3.652 | +0.001 |

GPU times are medians of seven samples, each timing 40 replays of a CUDA graph containing 64 scan calls. Baseline `e32e1238` and PR `06228625` used the same GB200 and container, with their respective built extensions.

# Checklist

- [x] I have read and followed the contributing guidelines
- [x] The functionality is complete for paths that run the multi-output scan
- [x] I have commented the device assertion and barrier behavior
- [x] I have made corresponding changes to the API documentation
- [x] My changes generate no new warnings
- [ ] I have added tests that prove the behavior
- [x] The focused existing tests pass locally

Summary

Adds device-side split alignment checks to the existing offset scan. The original C API keeps its behavior, while PyTorch callers can request alignment. - Grouped offset scans check each split against its requested alignment. Reviews (6) · Last reviewed commit: ["Apply suggestion from @timmoon10"](https://github.com/nvidia/transformerengine/commit/7e69595bce9a0ed57e489dd5eb435b122ee0a075) · [Reviewed by Greptile](https://www.greptile.com/?utm_source=greptile_review&utm_medium=github&utm_campaign=review_public&utm_content=nvidia/transformerengine)

**Key alignment cases remain untested** The new test uses only two splits in an ordinary launch. It never reaches the 256-thread scan, a later chunk, or CUDA graph replay. A regression that checks only the first chunk or only during capture could still pass. Add a case with more than 256 splits and an invalid value after index 255. Also capture a graph with valid splits, then make them misaligned before replay. Note: If this suggestion doesn't match your team's coding style, reply to this and let me know. I'll remember it for next time!

Is there reason to support separate kernels for these two cases? This kernel seems launch-bound, so the smaller variant doesn't give us much perf benefit.

I don't think we need to go into the implementation details. The contract is the user gives us aligned split sizes, and bad things happen if that's not the case.
```suggestion
        Expected alignment for input split sizes. Split sizes that do not
        match alignment may produce errors or incorrect results.
```

nodes.body: The improves perf by about 0.2 us. I would assume this is purely warp scheduling overhead (4 vs 8 warps). But at the scale of 2-3 us for the kernel that is 10% perf benefit. And so I kept this change. But you can see that we are loosing the perf by about 0.2 us due to the introduction of alginment check.
I evaluated this change. And not doing the bit masking costs us 0.07us consistently for the kernel.
NVTE_DEVICE_ERROR just does assert(0) and doesnt do a trap. so it ll be compiled away during prod builds
